title: Did you know… the difference between obedience and assumption can cost you everything?
paragraphs: Did you know… the difference between obedience and assumption can cost you everything?
But here’s what most people don’t realize…
The first time water came from the rock, God gave a very specific command.
“Take the staff… and tell the rock before their eyes to yield its water.” — Numbers 20:8
Tell the rock. Not strike it.
Dust in the air. Thirst everywhere. Panic rising.
God had already shown His power once before:
“And you shall strike the rock, and water shall come out of it, and the people will drink.” — Exodus 17:6
Different day. Same problem. No water.
But this time… a different command.
Because God was painting something deeper.
“They drank from the spiritual Rock… and the Rock was Christ.” — 1 Corinthians 10:4
“He was pierced for our transgressions… and by His wounds we are healed.” — Isaiah 53:5
Moses stood before the people—frustrated, angry, exhausted.
And instead of trusting God’s exact word…
He relied on what worked before.
“Hear now, you rebels: shall we bring water for you out of this rock?” — Numbers 20:10
“Because you did not believe in me, to uphold me as holy… you shall not bring this assembly into the land.” — Numbers 20:12
But Moses lost the Promised Land.
Striking the rock again misrepresented Christ.
“Christ was offered once to bear the sins of many.” — Hebrews 9:28
“If you confess with your mouth that Jesus is Lord and believe in your heart… you will be saved.” — Romans 10:9
🔥 But here’s what most people don’t realize…
You can still see results… and still be out of alignment.
You can still get “water”… and miss God’s holiness.
You don’t need to strike harder.
You don’t need to fix yourself.
“Come to me, all who labor and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest.” — Matthew 11:28
If this found you, it’s not by accident.
And when you're ready to go deeper—real discipleship, real transformation:
Where in your life are you repeating what God never told you to do again?
Because partial obedience is still disobedience.
And Jesus deserves more than habits…
